title: TCP: Add expert info for unusual flag combinations
description:
Add Expert Info for unusual TCP flag combinations commonly associated with scanning and fingerprinting.

Detect XMAS (FIN+PSH+URG), NULL (no control flags), and SYN+FIN combinations with dedicated, filterable expert fields.

The checks are stateless and independent of `tcp.analysis.flags`.

Add regression tests covering the expected combinations, supersets, and benign flag combinations.

changes_data.diff:
@@ -0,0 +1,168 @@
+#
+# Wireshark tests
+#
+# SPDX-License-Identifier: GPL-2.0-or-later
+#
+"""TCP flag-combination expert-info tests.
+
+Exercises the PF_FIN+PSH+URG (XMAS), NULL (no control flag), and SYN+FIN
+anomaly detection in epan/dissectors/packet-tcp.c against a synthetic
+Ethernet/IPv4/TCP capture generated in-memory with text2pcap.
+
+The capture carries twelve frames, one per flag combination studied:
+
+  Frame  flags                      expected expert
+     1   FIN+PSH+URG                  tcp.flags.xmas
+     2   (none)                       tcp.flags.null
+     3   SYN+FIN                      tcp.flags.syn_fin
+     4   SYN                          (none)
+     5   SYN+ACK                      (none)
+     6   SYN+ECE                      (none)
+     7   SYN+FIN+ACK                  tcp.flags.syn_fin   (superset included)
+     8   FIN+PSH+URG+ACK              tcp.flags.xmas       (superset included)
+     9   AE only                      (none)  -- AE is a control bit, so not NULL
+    10   ACK                          (none)
+    11   FIN+RST                      (none)  -- no dedicated rule
+    12   plain ACK with data         (none)
+
+The expected-set semantics are asserted per expert field: the filter
+tcp.flags.<x> must match exactly the frames in the expected set.
+"""
+
+import struct
+import subprocess
+
+# TCP flag bits, as read by packet-tcp.c (th_flags is the whole 12-bit field
+# at the TCP header offset 12, per TH_* constants in packet-tcp.h).
+TH_FIN  = 0x001
+TH_SYN  = 0x002
+TH_RST  = 0x004
+TH_PUSH = 0x008
+TH_ACK  = 0x010
+TH_URG  = 0x020
+TH_ECE  = 0x040
+TH_CWR  = 0x080
+TH_AE   = 0x100
+
+
+def _ip_checksum(header):
+    if len(header) % 2:
+        header += b'\x00'
+    total = 0
+    for i in range(0, len(header), 2):
+        total += (header[i] << 8) + header[i + 1]
+    while total >> 16:
+        total = (total & 0xffff) + (total >> 16)
+    return (~total) & 0xffff
+
+
+def _tcp_checksum(src, dst, tcp):
+    pseudo = struct.pack('!4s4sBBH', src, dst, 0, 6, len(tcp))
+    data = pseudo + tcp
+    if len(data) % 2:
+        data += b'\x00'
+    total = 0
+    for i in range(0, len(data), 2):
+        total += (data[i] << 8) + data[i + 1]
+    while total >> 16:
+        total = (total & 0xffff) + (total >> 16)
+    return (~total) & 0xffff
+
+
+def _tcp_frame(flags16, sport=12345, dport=443):
+    '''Build one Ethernet+IPv4+TCP frame with the given 12-bit flag value.'''
+    src = bytes([10, 0, 0, 1])
+    dst = bytes([10, 0, 0, 2])
+
+    ip = struct.pack('!BBHHHBBH4s4s', 0x45, 0, 40, 0x1234, 0, 64, 6, 0, src, dst)
+    csum = _ip_checksum(ip)
+    ip = ip[:10] + struct.pack('!H', csum) + ip[12:]
+
+    # byte 12 = [data offset(4) | control nibble(4)], byte 13 = flags.
+    # th_flags in the dissector is the 16-bit BE value at offset 12 (TH_MASK).
+    byte12 = (5 << 4) | ((flags16 >> 8) & 0x0f)
+    byte13 = flags16 & 0xff
+    tcp = struct.pack('!HHIIBBHHH', sport, dport, 1000, 0,
+                      byte12, byte13, 0x1000, 0, 0)
+    csum = _tcp_checksum(src, dst, tcp)
+    tcp = tcp[:16] + struct.pack('!H', csum) + tcp[18:]
+
+    eth = bytes.fromhex('00112233445566778899aabb') + struct.pack('!H', 0x0800)
+    return eth + ip + tcp
+
+
+# (flags16, [expected expert fields])
+_CASES = [
+    (TH_FIN | TH_PUSH | TH_URG,              {'tcp.flags.xmas'}),
+    (0,                                      {'tcp.flags.null'}),
+    (TH_SYN | TH_FIN,                        {'tcp.flags.syn_fin'}),
+    (TH_SYN,                                 set()),
+    (TH_SYN | TH_ACK,                        set()),
+    (TH_SYN | TH_ECE,                        set()),
+    (TH_SYN | TH_FIN | TH_ACK,               {'tcp.flags.syn_fin'}),
+    (TH_FIN | TH_PUSH | TH_URG | TH_ACK,     {'tcp.flags.xmas'}),
+    (TH_AE,                                  set()),
+    (TH_ACK,                                 set()),
+    (TH_RST | TH_FIN,                        set()),
+    (TH_ACK,                                 set()),
+]
+
+
+def _write_capture(cmd_text2pcap, pcap_path, txt_path):
+    with open(txt_path, 'w') as f:
+        for flags16, _exp in _CASES:
+            frame = _tcp_frame(flags16)
+            for i in range(0, len(frame), 16):
+                chunk = frame[i:i + 16]
+                f.write('{:04x}  {}\n'.format(i, ' '.join('%02x' % b for b in chunk)))
+            f.write('\n')
+    subprocess.check_call(
+        [cmd_text2pcap, txt_path, pcap_path],
+        stdout=subprocess.DEVNULL, stderr=subprocess.DEVNULL,
+    )
+
+
+def _matching_frames(cmd_tshark, pcap_path, test_env, field):
+    '''Return the set of frame numbers matching the given filter.'''
+    out = subprocess.check_output(
+        [cmd_tshark, '-r', pcap_path, '-Y', field, '-Tfields', '-e', 'frame.number'],
+        encoding='utf-8', env=test_env)
+    return {int(x) for x in out.split()}
+
+
+class TestTcpFlagCombinationExperts:
+    '''Verify the XMAS/NULL/SYN+FIN expert fields fire on exactly the
+    intended frames, with no false positives on benign flag use.'''
+
+    def _run(self, cmd_tshark, cmd_text2pcap, result_file, test_env, field):
+        pcap = result_file('pcap')
+        txt = result_file('txt')
+        _write_capture(cmd_text2pcap, pcap, txt)
+        return _matching_frames(cmd_tshark, pcap, test_env, field)
+
+    def test_xmas_only(self, cmd_tshark, cmd_text2pcap, result_file, test_env):
+        assert self._run(cmd_tshark, cmd_text2pcap, result_file, test_env,
+                         'tcp.flags.xmas') == {1, 8}
+
+    def test_null_only(self, cmd_tshark, cmd_text2pcap, result_file, test_env):
+        # AE-only (frame 9) is not NULL: AE is a control bit (RFC 9293).
+        assert self._run(cmd_tshark, cmd_text2pcap, result_file, test_env,
+                         'tcp.flags.null') == {2}
+
+    def test_syn_fin_only(self, cmd_tshark, cmd_text2pcap, result_file, test_env):
+        # SYN+FIN+ACK (frame 7) is intentionally included.
+        assert self._run(cmd_tshark, cmd_text2pcap, result_file, test_env,
+                         'tcp.flags.syn_fin') == {3, 7}
+
+    def test_no_false_positives(self, cmd_tshark, cmd_text2pcap,
+                                result_file, test_env):
+        # Frames 4/5/6 (plain establishment), 9 (AE-only), 10/12 (ACK),
+        # 11 (FIN+RST) must not trip any of the new experts.
+        pcap = result_file('pcap')
+        txt = result_file('txt')
+        _write_capture(cmd_text2pcap, pcap, txt)
+        for frame in (4, 5, 6, 9, 10, 11, 12):
+            for field in ('tcp.flags.xmas', 'tcp.flags.null', 'tcp.flags.syn_fin'):
+                out = _matching_frames(cmd_tshark, pcap, test_env, field)
+                assert frame not in out, \
+                    'frame %d unexpectedly matched %s' % (frame, field)

@@ -429,7 +429,7 @@ class TestText2pcapHeaders:

@@ -529,7 +529,7 @@ class TestText2pcapIpv6:

         '''Test TCP over IPv6'''
         assert {'encapsulation': 'ether', 'packets': 1, \
-            'datasize': 78, 'expert': '', \
+            'datasize': 78, 'expert': '\nWarns (1)\n=============\n   Frequency      Group           Protocol  Summary\n           1   Protocol                TCP  No TCP control flags set: unusual flag combination, commonly associated with NULL scanning\n', \

commits_data.title: TCP: Add expert info for unusual flag combinations
commits_data.message:
TCP: Add expert info for unusual flag combinations

Add Expert Info for unusual TCP control-flag combinations commonly
associated with scanning and fingerprinting.

Detect FIN+PSH+URG (XMAS), no control flags (NULL), and SYN+FIN
combinations. Keep the checks stateless and independent of
tcp.analysis.flags.

Add regression coverage using a synthetic text2pcap capture.

Signed-off-by: Urval Kheni <kheniurval777@gmail.com>
